editorial: We didn’t keep a clean end-to-end expense sheet, so there is no honest trip total to publish.

A few anchors from our trip are more useful anyway. Beach beds in Mirissa with drinks cost about 2,000 LKR per person. A good, simple meal at Savour Street in Colombo was around 1,200 LKR per person. Private taxis were our biggest recurring expense because we chose speed over public transport.
Sri Lanka felt good value overall, especially relative to how easy and polished the tourist experience was.

alternatives.title: What if we had a bigger budget?
editorial: We’d spend it on stays rather than more activities: a beautiful tea-country property around Ella or Nuwara Eliya, and a beachfront room in Mirissa where sunset requires no logistics.
We might also keep the private-car strategy throughout, because on a short trip time is the luxury that matters.

alternatives.title: What if we had a smaller budget?
editorial: Use trains and buses for the longer legs, stay in homestays and eat rice-and-curry meals at local restaurants. The headline experiences—Dambulla, Sigiriya, the Nine Arches walk and the beach—do not require luxury spending.
